en_note: Machine translation by Claude (my reading), not on Pesna.org and not checked by a native speaker. Treat it as a study aid.
translator_notes: Old urban song; 'аман' is a Turkish-origin cry, left as is. 'Мерак фрлам' I render 'throw my longing' (my reading); the third-person 'зеде, даде' in verse two is as sung.

lines.en: I am a young grocer,
I sell almonds and hazelnuts, aman!
I sell almonds and hazelnuts,

lines.cyr: парите ги земам во меана одам,
lines.lat: parite gi zemam vo meana odam,
lines.en: I take the money and go to the tavern,
I leave a tip for the musicians, aman!
I leave a tip for the musicians.

lines.cyr: Една ока лешник, три кила бадем,
lines.lat: Edna oka lešnik, tri kila badem,
lines.en: One oka of hazelnuts, three kilos of almonds,

lines.cyr: парите ги зеде, в' меана ги даде.
lines.lat: parite gi zede, v' meana gi dade.
lines.en: he took the money, he gave it away in the tavern.
Be quiet, hey Nada, make the snacks,
bring wine, brandy, aman!
Let the whole market drink.
I am a crazy grocer,
I drink wine, strong brandy, aman!
I drink wine, strong brandy,

lines.cyr: на убави моми мерак кога фрлам,
lines.lat: na ubavi momi merak koga frlam,
lines.en: I throw my longing at pretty girls,

lines.cyr: ишарет со око им давам, аман!
lines.lat: išaret so oko im davam, aman!
lines.en: I give them a sign with my eye, aman!
This is how I live my life.

bring wine, brandy, aman!
